item.description:
### Added - **Answer OpenCode 2 sessions from Perch.** Until now Perch could show that an OpenCode 2 session needed you, but not let you answer. Now you can: - Allow, Deny, or "Allow and don't ask again" a permission, from the Mac notification, the phone or the watch. "Don't ask again" saves OpenCode's own rule for the project, the same one OpenCode would save, and the button says which. - Answer a question from the phone when it offers choices, or from the Mac's notification when it asks for one line of text. A question Perch can't answer exactly stays in OpenCode. - Reply to a session that's idle or working, and Stop one that's working.
Every answer goes only to the OpenCode server on this Mac, and only if it is still the server the question came from. - **Claude: a model change shows straight away,** including one Claude makes by itself. - **Claude: an MCP server asking for input shows as needing you straight away,** instead of after a few quiet seconds. Perch doesn't offer a reply for these, because a typed reply could submit the server's form. - **Claude: a session in a folder you haven't trusted yet says so.** Claude runs no hooks there until you accept its trust prompt, so the row used to look broken. It now reads "Waiting for you to trust this folder", and becomes a normal row as soon as you accept.
### Fixed - **OpenCode Stats and the Go usage estimate count OpenCode 2.** After upgrading, they stopped at the upgrade date, and a fresh OpenCode 2 Mac showed nothing. Your history from before the upgrade is counted once, not twice. On a Mac running both OpenCode 1 and 2, sessions no longer appear and disappear depending on which one ran last. - **OpenCode 2: an answered prompt no longer comes back.** One answered while Perch's connection had dropped for a moment could show as needing you again later. - **Claude `-p` runs: approvals say what happens if nobody answers.** In a run with no terminal prompt to fall back to, Claude denies the tool when no answer comes. The Mac notification now says so, and the row stops showing "needs you" afterwards. The phone and watch get the same wording in the next iOS update. - **Claude: Perch won't type into the wrong conversation.** When a session runs without Perch's hooks, Perch guesses which conversation it is. If Claude's own record of that session disagrees, Perch now offers no reply instead of one that could land in another session. - **Claude background sessions say how to open them.** A running background session was told to "run in tmux or herdr", which can't help. It now says to open it with `claude attach`.
